text:
mei: quick note — brought Argus7b-lite (Mistral-ish) up on Dedicated and ran int4 conversion with our proj-order packer. Running summarization eval and seeing a reproducible quality regression vs the Llama baseline. Dumping short repro and observations.

raj: paste the eval cmd + one bad example pls

mei: eval cmd:
```
./eval/run_eval.sh --model argus7b-lite-int4 --suite summarization --batch 8 --seed 7
```
bad example (truncated):
User: Summarize the following support exchange into 3 bullets...
Expected: bullets about invoice misapplied, refund pending, owner to reach out
Observed: verbose repetition, wrong follow-up owner, lower factuality

tasha: did you check a straight fp16 export to isolate quant vs packing?

mei: yes. fp16 (no proj reorder, no int4) matches baseline. Regression only appears when int4 + proj re-pack applied.

harry: proj re-pack = we reshape/transpose and interleave q/k/v into kernel-friendly head order, right?

mei: correct. Converter does reshape->transpose->pack. If source used a nonstandard packing we may be mixing head groups across q/k/v which breaks attention math.

raj: also watch tokenizer/vocab mismatches. Argus has soft-hyphen folding and a slightly different emoji cluster policy — if kv-cache index assembly or pad alignment shifts ids, long-context addressing will be off.

mei: token diffs for short prompts align. For long-context cases I found occasional off-by-one at pad/eos boundaries after conversion. Snippet:
```
# fp16 ids:  2019  34  777  999  2
# int4 ids:  2019  34  777 1000  2  <- 999->1000 at eos pad
```

tasha: so two likely causes: a) weight layout remap altering attention computation, b) token id/pad handling shifting kv positions. Both would decrease quality but with different fingerprints.

harry: quick test: run int4 binary but tell runtime to interpret proj blocks using source ordering (no runtime remap). If quality returns, converter packing is wrong.

mei: running that now:
```
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_OVERRIDES=PROJ_READ_MODE=SOURCE
./serve_local.sh --model argus7b-lite-int4 --port 9123 --no-autobatch
```

ci-bot: deploy-check OK on 9123, health green, p95 86ms (local), queued eval.

mei: result: with PROJ_READ_MODE=SOURCE the summaries match baseline style for ~90% of cases. Regression strongly tied to proj packing.

raj: good find. Plan: 1) add converter per-layer projection-layout fingerprinting to detect nonstandard q/k/v packing and avoid automatic repack when uncertain; 2) add an eval unit test that compares next-token logits on short prefixes across fp16/int4 exports to catch silent math diffs.

tasha: short-term mitigation = expose converter flag to preserve source ordering and add a runtime shim to remap only when needed (avoid mass re-exports).

harry: I'll prototype shim. Idea: if header.proj_fingerprint != expected, load raw buffer and apply per-head slice remap R so that R @ W_packed == W_source. We already have similar code for head-concat cases. Perf hit should be small.

mei: note: even after shim we still see tiny residual long-context diffs — likely pad/eos id shift from tokenizer interaction. I'll open a follow-up triage to add emoji/soft-hyphen cases to kv-cache assembly tests.

raj: concrete actions:
- mei: open PRs: (A) converter fingerprint + --preserve-proj-order flag, (B) tokenization+kv-cache testcases with failing long-context samples (put samples in /eval/artifacts/argus7b-lite/).
- harry: implement runtime remap shim + run perf check (target <2% p95 regression).
- tasha: add eval guard to compute L2 diff on next-token logits for first 64 tokens across exports and fail if >1e-3.

mei: will upload artifacts and link PRs, thanks all :thumbsup:

harry: ping me for pair on remap math.

ci-bot: ticket created: #INFR-4321 "Argus7b-lite proj-layout conversion regression" assigned to mei/harry/raj, priority P2.
